context_quotes.quote: When NOS was ectopically expressed in PPL1-γ2α′1, the valence of the memory formed by the 3 × 1 min training protocol switched to positive.

evidence.quote: Activation of PPL1-γ2α'1 resulted in negative-valence memory in both TH mutant and wild type, suggesting a cotransmitter with the same sign of action as dopamine.

new_finding.label: AVERSIVE
new_finding.note: Single-type activation gives negative-valence memory in wild type; ectopic-NOS inversion recorded as context (provision 3).

alias_quotes.quote: PPL1-α′2/α′2 (MB-V1) does not respond to heat and shock (Kirkhart and Scott, 2015; Mao and Davis, 2009) and cannot induce aversive memory by itself, but can have a synergistic effect on memory retention when coactivated with PPL1-γ2α′1 (Aso and Rubin, 2016).

evidence.quote: In contrast, other DANs from the PPL1 cluster that do not exhibit significant NOS expression, PPL1-α3 or a combination of PPL1-γ2α'1 and PPL1-α'2α2, are able to induce stable memory lasting for 4 days after 10x spaced training (Aso and Rubin, 2016).

new_finding.label: UNRESOLVED
new_finding.note: M5D1B amendment provision 1: S6 states PPL1-α′2/α′2 (MB-V1) cannot induce aversive memory by itself; S3 confirms MB-V1 = PPL1-α′2α2 (line MB058B).

context_quotes.quote: Activation of PPL1-α3 or PAM-β'1 in the TH mutant background did not induce significant memory, indicating that these cells do not express a cotransmitter capable of inducing memory without dopamine.

evidence.quote: Note that activation of PPL1-α3 can induce negative-valence memory in a wild-type background, but only after 10x spaced training (Aso and Rubin, 2016).

new_finding.label: AVERSIVE
new_finding.note: Wild-type activation gives negative-valence memory after 10x spaced training; TH-mutant null result recorded as context (provision 3).
